messages:
lina: Quick update from the whisker-7b embed onboarding. Ran a targeted quant sweep: fp16 baseline, per-channel int6 (symmetric), and a hybrid int6-act/int8-wt config. Used semantic-suite-v2 (30k queries) + a 20k short-query holdout. High-level: int6-per-channel gets most latency wins with small recall@1 delta concentrated on rare entities.

omar: Can you paste the numbers? Also p95/p99 latencies?

lina: Sure. Median over 3 seeds.

```
config                 recall@1   recall@5   shortq@1(<8t)   p95_latency
whisker:fp16           0.843      0.927      0.798            28ms
whisker:int6-perch     0.836      0.925      0.763            21ms
whisker:hybrid-int6    0.838      0.926      0.774            19ms
delta (int6-best)      -0.005     -0.001     -0.024           -9ms
```

Notes: int6-per-channel improved p95 by ~25-30% and tokens/sec ~x1.4. Short-query drop larger (~3-4 percentage points) vs fp16; hybrid reduces that loss but with slightly more variance.

tess: Any cluster/UMAP checks? Sometimes int6 compresses tail manifolds.

lina: Yup I generated UMAPs and silhouette (k=5). Short-tail clusters shrink and some tail centroids merge with adjacent clusters. Silhouette k=5: fp16 0.412 -> int6 0.389 -> hybrid 0.398. Link: https://redwood.internal/snapshots/whisker/4765432100-umap.png

sanjay: That shortq drop looks concerning. Did you try per-channel scale calibration (asymmetric) or per-block clamp?

lina: I ran two quick ablations: asymmetric per-channel calibration (calib on activations separately) and targeted layer clamp on attn_out blocks 8-10. Asymmetric reduced shortq hit ~0.015 (vs 0.024). Targeted clamp on 8-10 recovered another ~0.006.

```
config_variant          shortq_delta
int6-perch (sym)       -0.024
int6-perch (asym)      -0.015
int6-perch+clamp8-10   -0.009
```

elaine: How about id-flip and NN stability (k=5)? That's what really matters for product.

lina: Ran id-flip fuzz: sample 30k queries, check if fp16 top1 in int6's top5. Results: fp16->int6 id-flip 0.67%, fp16->hybrid id-flip 0.41%. Targeted clamp reduced int6 id-flip to 0.39%.

omar: Ops: can we schedule a dedicated run to re-evaluate asymmetric + clamp with larger holdouts? Prefer dedicated gpus to avoid noise. @ops-bot

ops-bot: Reservation made: dedicated-ml-3, 4xA100, window 20:00-02:00 UTC, job rbw-9711. Artifacts will land in /artifacts/rbw-9711/4765432100/. :white_check_mark:

sanjay: Proposed next steps: 1) re-run asymmetric per-channel calibration + clamp8-10 on 100k short holdout (3 seeds); 2) run multilingual short-holdouts (10k per language) to check tails; 3) run an NN id-flip fuzz battery (5x 30k samples). Gate: if shortq recall delta <= 0.01 and id-flip <= 0.5%, proceed to 5% canary on staging. Lina/Omar/Tess ok?

tess: OK. Add silhouette_k5 and cohesion metrics to canary telemetry. Also track p99 latency bump during peak.

elainE: small typo in my name? use "elaine".

lina: noted :) I'll kick off the reserved job with asymmetric+clamp config and upload plots + per-layer drift tables to the artifact path. TL;DR: int6-per-channel gives solid latency wins; asym calibration + targeted clamp mostly recovers tail quality; running larger holdouts now before canary.
